Robot Doctor Vision

Camera or Limelight isn't detected

Not found in code, drops out, or returns nothing. Below are the 4 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 5 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Is it a Limelight 3A? The Limelight smart camera, rather than a USB webcam.
  • Does your code call limelight.start() and check result.isValid()? Search the code for "start()" on the Limelight.
  • Does the error say "Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..."? The red error text at the bottom of the Driver Station.
  • Does the camera disappear until you power cycle the robot? The camera stops showing up or vision returns nothing until a restart.
  • Do you have a grounding strap and all USB devices in the USB 3.0 port? The grounding strap is a short wire with a resistor from a spare XT30 port to the frame. The Control Hub's USB 3.0 port is the blue one.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Camera on the wrong port or underpowered

Cameras drop out from ESD on the USB 2.0 port, from too many USB devices, or from loose cables.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Use the Control Hub's USB 3.0 port.
  2. FIRST recommends powering at most 2 cameras directly over USB. Use a powered USB hub for more.
  3. Add strain relief and a ferrite choke to the camera cable.
  4. Check the webcam name in the configuration matches your code (often "Webcam 1").

Sources: FTC Docs · Configuring a webcam · FTC Docs · Managing ESD · FTC Docs · Power management

2 Limelight not configured or started

The Limelight 3A needs to be in the configuration and started in code before it returns results.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Add it to the Robot Controller configuration (Limelight3A) and use the same name in code.
  2. Call pipelineSwitch(...) and limelight.start() before reading results.
  3. Always check result != null && result.isValid() before using the data.
  4. It draws power whenever the hub is on, even with no OpMode running, so keep the battery charged.
Limelight basics
Limelight3A limelight = hardwareMap.get(Limelight3A.class, "limelight");
limelight.setPollRateHz(100);
limelight.pipelineSwitch(0);
limelight.start();

LLResult result = limelight.getLatestResult();
if (result != null && result.isValid()) {
    double tx = result.getTx();
}

Sources: Limelight · FTC programming · FTC Docs · Configuring a webcam

3 Name in code doesn't match the configuration

"Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..." means the string in hardwareMap.get is not exactly the name in the active configuration.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Open the configuration on the Driver Station and compare names letter by letter. They are case sensitive ("leftDrive" is not "LeftDrive").
  2. Make sure the configuration you edited is the active one (its name shows on the DS main screen) and that you saved it.
  3. Watch for trailing spaces in config names.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

4 Static shock (ESD) from the field

Robots build static driving on tiles. When the frame touches metal, the discharge can reset the hub, the IMU, the camera, or Wi-Fi.

How to fix it 30 min

  1. Notice whether it happens right after touching a field element or another robot. That pattern is classic ESD.
  2. Install a FIRST-legal resistive grounding strap (REV-31-1269) from a spare XT30 port to the frame.
  3. Plug cameras and other USB devices into the Control Hub's USB 3.0 port. The USB 2.0 port has a known ESD issue that can knock out Wi-Fi.
  4. Mount electronics on a non-conductive panel (thin plywood, PVC) and keep exposed connector metal more than 3/8" (1 cm) from the frame. Arcs can jump that far.
  5. Snap ferrite chokes onto sensor, encoder, servo, and USB cables, and tape over exposed metal on servo extensions.
  6. Things touching the floor (foam wheels, a dragging intake) build static faster. Many teams wipe the robot with a dryer sheet between matches.

Sources: FTC Docs · Managing ESD · REV · General troubleshooting · GM0 · Wiring guide
